questions.prompt: Match each food to its preservation method.
questions.explain: Each method stops or slows microbes.

questions.prompt: How does a refrigerator keep food fresh longer?
options: It slows down the growth of microbes
questions.explain: Microbes survive but grow very slowly in the cold.

questions.prompt: Why do salt and sugar preserve food?
options: They draw water out of microbes so they can't grow
heated to about 70 °C for a short time and then cooled quickly
questions.explain: This kills most harmful microbes without spoiling the taste. It is named after Louis Pasteur.

questions.prompt: In the Food Preserver, which kept the dal safe the longest (without salting, sugaring or drying)?
options: Left out in a warm kitchen
questions.explain: Boiling reduces the starting number of microbes; cold slows the rest.

questions.prompt: Bacteria in warm food double every 30 minutes. Starting with 100, how many are there after 3 hours?
About a third of all food produced is wasted, some of it through spoilage. Suggest how better food preservation could help farmers in India, and one challenge.
questions.modelAnswer: Cold storage and refrigerated transport would let farmers store fruit and vegetables for longer, so they don't have to sell everything at once at low prices, and less food rots on the way to markets. Drying, pickling and making jams add value to extra produce. Challenges: cold storage needs reliable electricity and money to build; small farmers may not be able to afford it; transport in hot weather is difficult.
rubric: How preservation reduces spoilage or waste
questions.explain: Criterion D: link science to food security.

questions.text: Illness caused by eating food spoiled by microbes is called food ___.
questions.explain: Some spoiled food looks and smells fine but is still unsafe.
